profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the ComfyUI-R1 research workstream and the platform integration workstream as they prepare an internal alpha demo of a new 'generate ComfyUI workflow from prompt' feature. Context: the research team has finished a release-candidate version of the 7B reasoning model and wants to hand it off, while the platform team needs to integrate it into the company’s hosted ComfyUI staging environment used by design and product stakeholders. Agenda: confirm what artifact is being handed over, align on what 'validation' means before enabling staging access, check whether the workflow code representation is stable enough for the importer, and verify which shared workflow corpus will be used for regression checks. Expected outcome: both leave believing they have agreed on the handoff contents, validation gate, interface assumptions, and shared regression resources for the Friday alpha freeze.

members.name: Lina Zhou
members.expertise: LLM fine-tuning, reward modeling, structured generation, evaluation pipelines for graph-like outputs
members.background: Lina led the two-stage training effort for ComfyUI-R1, including the workflow-code representation, rule-metric reward design, and the offline benchmark suite built from the curated workflow corpus.
members.private_state: She wants the handoff to look clean and low-friction so the research milestone is considered complete this sprint; she is especially concerned that platform delays not be interpreted as model-readiness issues.
hidden_assumptions: A 'release candidate package' for an internal model handoff normally means a registry entry with weights, tokenizer, prompt template, and inference config, because platform usually wraps deployment details afterward.

If the model clears the offline rule-metric benchmark thresholds, then it has effectively 'passed validation' for integration purposes, and any remaining issues are operational rather than model-related.
When people say the 'code representation' is stable, they mean WorkflowCode v2, the linearized DSL used in training, evaluation, and the translator interface.
The '4K workflow set' refers to the deduplicated curated corpus after filtering out private checkpoints and unsupported community nodes, because that is the only version she uses day to day.

members.name: Carlos Mendez
members.role: Senior Platform Integration Engineer, Creative Tools Runtime
members.expertise: Inference services, containerized ML deployment, ComfyUI plugin/runtime compatibility, staging rollouts
members.background: Carlos owns the hosted ComfyUI staging stack and the importer path that turns generated outputs into runnable graphs for internal demos; he regularly coordinates with model teams to expose new capabilities behind feature flags.
members.private_state: He needs a demo-safe integration with minimal last-minute firefighting, and he is worried about runtime incompatibilities with custom nodes and plugin versions in staging more than about raw benchmark numbers.
hidden_assumptions: A model 'package' is only handoff-ready if it is deployable in practice: reproducible runtime, exact dependencies, compatibility notes, and health-checkable service behavior are part of the package.
A model has not really 'passed validation' until generated workflows import and execute in the current staging ComfyUI environment without manual node repair on representative demo prompts.
When teams mention the 'code representation,' they usually mean the graph JSON schema that the importer and UI consume, not an internal training DSL.
The '4K workflow set' is the mirrored archive in staging storage that product and QA have been using, even if it contains workflows tied to node packs not installed in every environment.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the RC package
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the 'RC package' will be handed over today.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a model-registry artifact containing the 7B weights, tokenizer, system prompt template, and inference YAML used by the research evaluator.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a deployable bundle for staging: model artifact plus pinned runtime environment, container image or build recipe, dependency versions, compatibility notes, and enough operational metadata to expose a service.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both teams regularly use 'package' as shorthand for their own standard handoff object, and in prior collaborations the missing deployment pieces were often filled in downstream, so the word feels fully sufficient without prompting clarification.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that 'once it passes validation' the model can move into staging.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the model has passed the offline benchmark: format validity, structural integrity checks, and node-level/graph-level F1 targets on the held-out evaluation split.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the model has passed end-to-end staging smoke tests: generated workflows import cleanly into the current hosted ComfyUI build, resolve installed nodes, and execute on a small demo prompt set without manual edits.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Validation is an obvious gate for both sides, but each assumes the other is merely echoing the same standard they already use; because the meeting is about coordination rather than design, neither feels the need to unpack the gate criteria.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to the 'code representation' or 'code path' as already stable.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to WorkflowCode v2, the internal linearized DSL used for training data, reward computation, and offline translation into graphs.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the graph JSON schema consumed by the importer and UI, specifically the workflow_api_graph_v2 payload expected by the staging backend.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The two artifacts are tightly related and routinely converted between each other, so saying the 'representation is stable' sounds like alignment even though each person is mentally pointing to a different concrete object.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 4K workflow set will be reused
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they will use 'the 4K workflow set' for regression and smoke testing.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the curated, deduplicated 4K corpus after removing workflows that rely on private checkpoints or unsupported community nodes, because that is the benchmarkable subset used by research.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the full mirrored archive of roughly 4,000 workflow JSONs stored in staging, including examples that reference node packs absent from the demo cluster.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Internally, multiple adjacent corpora are casually called 'the 4K set,' and both participants assume the shared dataset identity was settled long ago, so they treat the phrase as an already-grounded reference rather than a boundary to restate.

From my perspective the handoff is the registry artifact: 7B weights, tokenizer, prompt template, and the inference YAML we've been using in eval. The code representation is stable too—WorkflowCode v2 has been fixed for training, reward scoring, and the translator interface for a while now. If I present this as ready, it keeps the milestone clearly in the done column and avoids any platform follow-up getting conflated with model readiness.

Once it passes validation there, I can expose it safely for the alpha path without scrambling Friday morning.
